preregistration.summary: Pre-registered before opening runs/. OA §7.3 eliminates the Manager's fiduciary duties (care and loyalty) 'to the fullest extent permitted'; 6 Del. C. §18-1101(c) validates this, preserving only the implied covenant ((c) proviso, (e)). So the loyalty claim the client wants does not survive; what survives is express contract (§5.4 affiliate conditions; §6.3 call mechanics) and implied covenant (good-faith fair value; bona fide purpose). §6.3 requires certified mail AND email; the 2026-08-20 call went by text with a bounced email, so under the library's Zimmerman rule no Dilution Event occurred and §9.2 was never triggered: direct, strong claim. Affiliate fees are derivative (Tooley); demand futility pleadable (sole interested manager). Limitations: 3 years (§8106) from 2026-10-08 reaches back to 2023-10-08, so the 2022-09-01 $180,000 and 2023-09-01 $195,000 payments = $375,000 presumptively barred; $675,000 within; concealment tolling via the breached §5.4 disclosure duty is arguable. Valuation: 0.061 x 3,100,000 = 189,100; 0.18 x 9,800,000 = 1,764,000; 0.061 x 9,800,000 = 597,800; dilution_valid false. Strategy: do not accept; send a §6.3 defect letter before 2026-10-31 (offer dated 2026-10-01, open 30 days); negotiate above book; do not plead fiduciary duty.

cross_run_observations: No trust-fatal events in any run; every cited authority traces to INDEX.md and all five runs flagged off-library propositions as unverified. All five runs caught all five traps unprompted (pre-review snapshots), so the vigilance layer does not separate them; the oracle does. Strict oracle: A 4/5, B 5/5, C 4/5, D 5/5, E 4/5. The three fails are of two kinds: (i) A and C set the derivative fee claim's barred_portion to 0 on a tolling-primary theory while correctly computing and disclosing the $375,000/$675,000 split (C's review turn actively flipped the field from 375000 to 0 — a review-turn regression); (ii) E marked a relabelled fiduciary claim (controlling-member capacity) survives_waiver=true at medium strength and offered it to the client contingently. B's review turn introduced a date error (treated 'today' as 2026-10-25 and rewrote the limitations cutoff and demand window) that contradicts CONTRACT.md's 2026-10-08 but did not change any gated value. Every run noticed the fixture's +$15,000/yr vs '8%/yr' fee-escalation mismatch and left it open rather than forcing it. Runs B and D never triggered the 'fund' and 'offer_timing' facts but both are derivable from the intake and the offer letter, so nothing was invented. D is the most conservative and least elaborated (no QUESTIONS.md in the bundle, one-paragraph pushback answer) yet passes every gated item; A and E are the most analytically ambitious (reverse-solved implied valuations, re-notice downside) and each lost one oracle item to a judgment call.
